known_limitations: safe_getattr on a dataclass field reads only the instance __dict__, so a field absent from an unpickled checkpoint config returns the caller's default, not the class-level default that plain getattr falls back to. test_G1_C7_safe_getattr requires this. Other attributes (properties, non-dataclass objects) use getattr(obj, name, default).

compare_dataclasses skips fields absent on both sides; a field absent on one side is reported as a difference with an internal sentinel, which update_config_with_changed_values never applies. update_config_with_changed_values also skips a difference whose parent section is absent on the target. Both cases raised AttributeError before; paths that already worked are unchanged.

backfill_missing_fields (unchanged) uses hasattr, so it does not backfill simple-default fields absent from an instance __dict__ (the class attribute makes hasattr true); reads of those still get the class default through plain getattr. Not changed here (outside T1.1 scope).
